title: Higgsino-like inelastic dark matter confronting the LZ event
question: What Higgsino mass, splitting and Z-mediated inelastic cross-section give one LZ event, and is that consistent with the paper's two-sided intervals, LEP/LHC bounds, loop-level elastic limits and the relic density?
headline_result: A pure Higgsino (sigma_n = 7.4e-39 cm^2, fixed by G_F) gives one LZ event only for delta = 358-380 keV at 1 TeV (best 366 keV; 336-351 keV at 500 GeV, 366-394 keV at 4 TeV), requiring 3-30 PeV gauginos; excluded at every tabulated delta <= 350 keV (x226 too many events at 300 keV, x1.9 at 350 keV); the thermal mass 1.1 TeV lies inside the window.
key_numbers: sigma_n=7.40e-39 cm^2; sigma_SI,eq=2.30e-39 cm^2; (c_eq m_v^2)^2=0.0777; vector factor 3.214; N(1 TeV)=790/11.1/0.49 at delta=300/350/370 keV; delta(N=1)=310,342,366,375,376 keV for 300-4000 GeV; delta_max(248 keV)=316-409 keV; M1=5.3-6.5 PeV (bino-only); June/Dec=46 (1 TeV); next 1000 live days 4-5 events; implied N at LZ upper edges 3.2-3.8 (Sun-frame halo)
model_or_mechanism: pure Higgsino doublet, Z-exchange chi1->chi2 inelastic O1 (isovector-dominated), splitting from PeV bino/wino mixing
